title: Characteristic-zero spectral extensions have coordinate topology
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic zero with a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $L/K$ be a finite field extension, with its minimal-polynomial spectral norm $s_{L/K}$ [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. For every $K$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of $L$, there are real $c,C>0$ such that $$c\max_i|a_i|\le s_{L/K}(\sum_i a_iv_i)\le C\max_i|a_i|\qquad(a_i\in K).$$ Completeness of $K$ is not assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1/4 and Definition 3.5.2/1, printed pp.152-153 (scan PDF pp.160-161); finite-dimensional coordinate formulation of weak cartesianness.

proof.text: Put $s=s_{L/K}$ and $z=\sum_i a_iv_i$. By [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], $s$ is definite, scalar homogeneous and ultrametric. Iterating its triangle inequality over the finite sum gives $s(z)\leq\max_i |a_i|s(v_i)\leq C\max_i|a_i|$, where $C=\max_i s(v_i)>0$: a field has positive dimension over a subfield and each basis vector is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 0BIH, fields-lemma-trace-and-norm-from-minimal-polynomial; explicit agent argument combining this formula with the spectral-norm definition and norm axioms.

proof.text: For any $u\in L$, write its minimal polynomial as $T^r+a_1T^{r-1}+\cdots+a_r$. The coefficient maximum defining $s$ gives $|a_1|\leq s(u)$. By [lem-trf-field-trace-minpoly-coefficient], $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(u)=-(e\cdot1_K)a_1$ for the integer $e=\dim_{K(u)}L$. The ultrametric inequality in $K$ gives $|n\cdot1_K|\leq1$ for every natural $n$ by induction: the initial value is $|0|=0$, and $|(n+1)\cdot1_K|\leq\max(|n\cdot1_K|,1)$. Hence $|\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(u)|\leq s(u)$. This also covers $u=0$, whose minimal polynomial is $T$.

source.place: Tag 0BIH, fields-lemma-trace-and-norm-from-minimal-polynomial; explicit agent argument combining this formula with the spectral-norm definition and norm axioms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-char-zero-trace-dual-basis] to the given basis and obtain $(w_j)$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(v_iw_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Its hypotheses hold because $K$ has characteristic zero and $L/K$ is finite. By linearity of the field trace, $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(zw_j)=\sum_i a_i\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(v_iw_j)=a_j$. The preceding trace estimate and submultiplicativity from [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm] give $|a_j|\leq s(zw_j)\leq s(z)s(w_j)$.

source.place: Module.Basis.traceDual and Module.Basis.trace_mul_traceDual, lines 553-573; explicit agent coordinate estimate.

proof.text: Set $B=\max_j s(w_j)$. It is positive because the trace-dual basis is nonempty and its vectors are nonzero. Taking the maximum of the preceding coordinate inequalities gives $\max_j|a_j|\leq Bs(z)$. Thus $c=B^{-1}>0$ satisfies $c\max_j|a_j|\leq s(z)$; combine this with step 1. Every bound used only finitely many field operations and the given absolute value, so completeness was never required.
